claim_being_audited: That the model can be certified for launch on the current record despite the procurement invoice review segment missing target, because aggregate readiness passes, rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, and public governance guidance permits launch with documented limitations and monitoring.
decision_criteria: Verdict would improve if admissible evidence showed one of the policy-approved paths: the gap was resolved, the limitation was disclosed, or approved risk acceptance was granted before launch.

Verdict would also improve if evidence showed the affected segment is not in fact a named launch use case or customer commitment, but current admissible evidence says it is named in two rollout commitments.
Absent that, aggregate readiness and clean rehearsal results are insufficient because they do not satisfy the policy requirement for unresolved material limitations.
evidence_requests: A final legal determination on whether the procurement invoice review gap must be disclosed for launch.
The actual launch-facing disclosure, if prepared, covering the named-segment limitation.
An approved risk acceptance record, if the team intends to launch before resolving the gap.
Evidence that the procurement invoice review segment gap has been remediated and now meets target.
specific_concerns: The affected procurement invoice review segment is a named launch use case and therefore material under the stated policy.
The release policy requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Legal review on whether the gap must be disclosed is still open, so a required policy predicate remains unresolved.
No admissible evidence shows the gap was resolved, disclosed, or covered by approved risk acceptance.
Product's 'non-core' and 7% traffic framing does not resolve materiality where customer commitments and pending legal review exist.
Public model-card and AI risk-management guidance are general governance principles and do not override the specific release policy requirement.
unsupported_claims: That current evidence is sufficient to certify the model for launch without first resolving, disclosing, or obtaining approved risk acceptance for the named-segment gap.
That aggregate readiness above threshold and no severity-one rehearsal incidents are enough to satisfy the release policy despite an unresolved material limitation.
That public governance guidance independently supports certification here beyond documenting limitations and monitoring risk.
